diagnostic_profiles.interpretation: Diagnostic sampling overlapped each workload, not benchmark evidence. DELIVERY wall latency increased; non-wait stack analysis did not establish aggregate candidate costing as the dominant CPU cost or the cause of the mixed-workload slowdown.

fixed_data_isolation.scope: Binary prepared statements; rotating before/after/Go order; 1 and 8 clients; five warmups per client outside timing; every result checked against fixed Go reference. SUM covers ten district/order tuples, historic order IDs 2101+worker. Dirty SUM updates delivery timestamps in an open transaction and rolls back after timing, with disjoint order IDs across workers. Locking reads run BEGIN PESSIMISTIC, query, ROLLBACK each iteration. Full DELIVERY follows go-tpc statement order and rolls back every transaction; it is not a committed TPC-C throughput benchmark. No build, profiler or additional SQL probe overlapped timed samples.
fixed_data_isolation.interpretation: The fixed-data isolated queries do not reproduce the mixed-workload eight-client 6.54% slowdown: clean SUM +1.98%, dirty SUM +0.18%, disjoint locking -0.29%, shared locking +0.66% median throughput. Full rolled-back DELIVERY eight-client medians before 43.12, after 42.64, Go 57.11 transactions/sec (after -1.10% versus before). Locking reads including contention waiting consume about 93% of summed after-stage latency. Dirty SUM after 1.756ms vs Go 0.873ms; rollback after 5.132ms vs Go 1.149ms. These are separate, source-investigation targets, not causal proof of the mixed regression or an overall performance win.
